newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chinese troops drill to block 1997 border stampede.
newsitem.headline: Chinese troops drill to block 1997 border stampede.

text.p: China has mounted a large-scale security exercise near Hong Kong to prepare its troops to cope with any sudden storming of the border by Chinese citizens when the British colony reverts to Beijing's control next year.

The semi-official China News Service said about 2,000 police and border troops in China's Guangdong province launched a drill on Tuesday with armoured cars, anti-riot units, ambulances and police dogs grouped in battle formations.
The officers fought for about an hour against crowds who staged a mock storming of the border, the agency said.

In another report, the China-controlled newspaper Wen Wei Po said on Wednesday that Hong Kong and Guangdong plan a joint security exercise designed to prevent any illegal stampede of Chinese into the territory at the time of the handover.
Wen Wei Po did not say when the exercise would take place.
The Hong Kong government's spokesman had no immediate comment on the report of planned joint exercises but said he was checking with security authorities.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China's control at midnight on June 30, ending a century and a half of colonial rule.

Newspaper reports over the past year have said many mainland Chinese think the handover means they can enter Hong Kong at will, while in fact China plans to keep the territory as a distinct entity and to continue to restrict immigration tightly.
Tuesday's exercise was aimed at ramming home the message that border controls will not disappear after Britain hands the colony over to China, Wen Wei Po said.
The Chinese province had conducted seven major border drills this year, it said.
Many mainland Chinese yearn to emigrate to Hong Kong where living standards are higher than in China. Illegal immigration is a constant problem for Hong Kong border police.
